subject: Food Science
title: Food Safety Audits
description: A fast breakdown of Food Safety Audits for builders.

hook.text: A single failed audit can cost a food company its largest customer overnight. Retailers demand third-party certification.

buildup.text: Audits evaluate a facility's compliance with BRCGS, SQF, or FSSC 22000—covering hygiene to documentation.

discovery.text: Auditors check everything: calibration logs, pest control records, allergen separation, employee training, and supplier approvals.

twist.text: Unannounced audits reveal real practices. Scheduled audits often get temporary cleanups that vanish the next day.

climax.text: GFSI (Global Food Safety Initiative) benchmarks audit schemes. Major retailers accept only GFSI-recognized certifications.

punchline.text: Audits don't test food. They test whether the system can consistently produce it safely.

quiz.question: What do food safety audits actually evaluate?
options: Whether the facility's systems can consistently produce safe food
